nate: Noticing a new regression on nova-q int8 canary when we ask multi-step agents to return 'plan' as an array of steps. Outputs sometimes serialize as object with string indices + occasional key order flip. Example: 

Expected:
{"plan":[{"act":"ask","args":{"q":"pricing"}},{"act":"fetch","args":{"id":10}}]}

Observed:
{"plan":{"1":{"act":"fetch","args":{"id":10}},"0":{"act":"ask","args":{"q":"pricing"}}}}

gabi: Huh. So it's an object instead of array and ordering is reversed. Validator flags this and downstream pipeline treats order; causing wrong tool invocation order.

priya: Any quant pattern?

nate: Only in int8 and on small-sequence runs with batch_size>=8. FP16 is clean.

canary-bot: canary snapshot: nova-q int8 plan_keymap_rate: 2.1% over 12h, fp16 0.03%

gabi: Could be serialization emitter using map literal when array indices are high-entropy tokens under quant quantization noise. Two mitigations: parser rehydrate (convert numeric-keyed maps to arrays) and enforce ordered-array contract in the postprocess stage that sorts keys numerically.

priya: Sorting keys numerically might mask real semantic ordering differences if model intentionally produced a map. But our schema says array. So conservative repair: only rehydrate when keys are exactly contiguous 0..n-1 and no extra fields.

nate: I ran a replay of 1.5k failing traces: rehydrate would have fixed 68% and introducing no semantic mismatches on manual spot-checks.

gabi: Add header X-Repaired: rehydrate-plan when applied. Also store raw+fixed pair to s3://eng-ml/quarantine/plan-repairs with 200/hr cap and PII redaction.

priya: Let's also run a quick bench across batch sizes to see correlation. I'll trigger eval-runner: 
```nrun-eval --model nova-q --quant int8 --suite agent-plan-suite --samples 5000 --tags batch_size,kvcache --out /tmp/novaq_int8_plan.jsonl
```

nate: Triage plan: 1) short-term: ship rehydrate behind feature flag to 2% traffic with logging + header. 2) mid-term: bench quant profiles and tune sampling/temperature for canary. 3) long-term: add model-side constraint during decoding to prefer array token sequences for array fields.

gabi: I'll PR the postprocess rehydration today with unit tests. priya can own the bench.

canary-bot: deploy scheduled: nova-q-int8 rehydrate-flag -> 2% at 2026-03-26T09:00Z by @gabi

priya: Also surface template_id and route in repaired telemetry so prompt teams can be notified.

nate: Great. Please tag @platform when you roll further; we may want a runtime knob to adjust batch_size defaults for tool-heavy routes.

gabi: ack.
